messages:
sam: Heads-up — ran a canary FP8 build against 3 nodes (batching=auto, kv_cache=enabled). Seeing a 20-35% per-token latency jitter at long contexts (~2048). Posting profiler dump and notes. :eyes:

ana: Thanks Sam. Can you paste the per-token breakdown? is this across both attention and matmul paths?

sam: paste below. short summary: matmul FP8 path shows higher variance when kv cache hit ratio drops below ~85%. attention kernel counters show fallback to FP16 for some ops (calibration mismatch).

jordan: interesting — did we hit the new hybrid-kernel selector? (--kernel-selector=hybrid-v2)

sam: yes. command: `./serve --model gptx-13b --quant fp8 --kernel-selector hybrid-v2 --batcher auto`

maria: profiler snippet (trimmed):
```
PER-TOKEN BREAKDOWN (median / p95)
kv_fetch: 0.7ms / 1.9ms
matmul_quant: 1.1ms / 3.6ms
attention_fp8: 0.9ms / 2.8ms
softmax: 0.2ms / 0.6ms
postproc: 0.3ms / 0.9ms
TOTAL: 3.2ms / 9.8ms

KERNEL COUNTERS:
matmul_fp8: 51234
matmul_int8: 1234
matmul_fp16_fallback: 768
attention_fp8: 49876
attention_fp16_fallback: 1245
cache_hits: 42189
cache_misses: 7321

NOTES: p95 dominated by matmul_fp8 tail and kv_fetch spikes when cache_miss rate increases.
```

kevin: Looks like calibration drift — some layers are triggering fp16 fallback. Which calibration profile was used?

sam: `calib_profile=autotune-2026-03-10` — we ran both static and dynamic calibration. static had fewer fallbacks but slightly worse output quality on eval set. dynamic lowered quality regressions but triggered more fallback heuristics at runtime when activations exceeded calibrated range.

ana: So dynamic calibration reduces off-nominal quality but increases runtime kernel switching? That explains jitter. Any logs showing the exact fallback reason?

sam: yes — log excerpt: `kernel_select: layer=19 reason=out_of_range activation_max=127.3 calib_max=120.0 -> fallback=fp16`

maria: That line is the smoking gun. When activation_max > calib_max it forces FP16, and our kernel selector doesn't prefetch that decision, so we pay a scheduling cost + different kernel runtime.

jordan: Could we patch the selector to precompute fallback plan per-request using a short prefix pass (first 32 tokens) to detect likely layer overflows and choose consistent kernels?

sam: idea: run a micro-probe on the KV fetch path for long contexts only. If we detect high variance in activations early, lock to fp16 for remainder of request to avoid mid-request switches. Tradeoff: higher per-token cost but lower jitter.

kevin: Batching heuristics may amplify this — small micro-batches get mixed kernel choices within a batch leading to serialized launches. We should ensure kernel coalescing: coerce batch members to same kernel if mixing would cause stalls.

maria: Agreed. Two-prong mitigation: 1) improve calibration (wider dynamic range) 2) kernel coalescing in the batcher. Both short and long term.

sam: Quick numbers from a controlled run:
```
CONFIG A: fp8 + dynamic calib + no-coalesce
median: 3.2ms total
p95: 9.8ms total

CONFIG B: fp8 + dynamic calib + coalesce-by-kernel
median: 3.4ms total
p95: 5.1ms total (down ~48%)

CONFIG C: fp16 locked for request (no mid-switch)
median: 3.9ms total
p95: 4.3ms total
```

jordan: So coalescing gives the best latency tail without changing model precision too much. Nice. Any quality regressions measured for config B?

sam: eval set: config B has identical metrics to config A within noise (delta<0.2%), since we only coalesce kernel execution ordering, not precision per se.

ana: Are there memory or throughput tradeoffs? coalescing may increase latency for some requests if it waits to align kernels.

maria: Our batcher already has a 2ms wait window. Coalescing can piggyback on that. For live traffic we should make coalescing adaptive: only coalesce if p95 latency of recent window > threshold or cache_miss_rate > x%.

kevin: Also want visibility in Console: per-token kernel counters + cache hit ratio per route + per-request kernel-switch events. We need dashboards and an alert rule when kernel_switch_rate > 1% across a 5m window.

sam: added RN-4291 to infra: <https://redwood.ai/issue/4291|RN-4291> — dashboard panels for `kernel_counters`, `cache_hit_ratio`, and `kernel_switch_rate`.

maria: For observability we should emit structured events when a request triggers a fallback: `fallback_event: {request_id, layer, reason, activation_max, calib_max, chosen_kernel}` — even if logs are text, we should push these to metrics as counters with tags.

jordan: I can add lightweight metrics to the runtime. Will PR today. Also adding a `kernel_decision` histogram per-layer.

ana: For rollout plan: stage 1) enable coalescing on canary traffic (10%) with existing fp8. stage 2) add kernel-switch alerting and fallback event metrics. stage 3) iterate on calibration profiles and consider layer-wise wider ranges for layers 15-22 which are the hotspots.

sam: Agreed. Action items:
- jordan: PR for kernel_decision histogram + fallback counter (due EOD)
- maria: dashboard draft (RN-4291)
- kevin: batcher coalescing prototype (toggle flag)
- ana: run longitudinal eval for config B vs A (100k requests) and post diffs

kevin: I'll push the prototype behind `--coalesce-kernel` and enable on 10% canary.

ana: Thanks all. This feels like a clear plan. :thumbsup:

latency-bot: Incident check: no current SLA violations in the last 1h for canary nodes.

sam: I'll follow up with the full profiler logs and a small flamegraph export later today.

maria: ping me when flamegraphs are up, I'll annotate hotspot layers.

jordan: PR linked: <https://redwood.ai/pr/10234|add-kernel-decision-metrics>

sam: closing the loop here — will update thread after canary run.

maria: :rocket:
